problem: OK: sheriff star badge is iconic, readable, kid-friendly, and belongs to Frontier Town.
OK: pointed boots with spurs and stitched shafts have a strong Wild West silhouette.
Minor: the trough belongs in the town, but the category 3 background was too abstract for an outdoor main-street surface.
fix: Kept the object and surface, changed the background treatment to a blurred frontier storefront exterior.

problem: OK: covered wagon is iconic and clearly sits in the Frontier Town street environment.
OK: horseshoe is a strong Wild West icon and readable as a floating hand-sized object.
fix: Kept, with a sharper concrete marker.

problem: Category 3 used diagonal stripes, which is a category 1/2 background treatment. The potted cactus is physically fine on a boardwalk, but it needed a matching town backdrop.
fix: Kept the potted saguaro and boardwalk surface, changed the background to a blurred frontier storefront exterior.

problem: OK: honda loop and coiled rope silhouette make it read as a lasso, not a generic rope.
OK: sheriff office with a star emblem is clear architecture inside the town environment and uses no text.
OK: saddle on a stand is a complete freestanding object with strong western markers.
Batwing swinging doors read as saloon doors, which risks an alcohol association, and a doorway fragment is less satisfying as a single object.
fix: Replaced with a whole hitching rail on the dusty ground beside the boardwalk, using horseshoe caps and a tied lasso as the theme marker.

problem: OK: gold pouch with visible nuggets and a pickaxe clasp reads Gold Rush clearly.
The oil lantern was too generic; the tiny nugget charm would disappear at thumbnail size, and the red object on orange background had weak contrast.
fix: Rebuilt it as a lantern locked into a chunky crossed-pickaxe stand and changed the background to green.

problem: OK object and surface: tin coffee pot on campfire stones belongs in the creekside camp. Background rhythm needed adjustment after color fixes.
fix: Kept the object and surface, changed the background color to peach and used a blurred creekside camp backdrop.

problem: OK: prospector tent is big, readable, and clearly inside the Gold Rush camp environment.
OK: pickaxe with a visible nugget is a clear Gold Rush tool, not a weapon.
OK: ore cart with gold rocks and chunky rail base is readable mining transport.
A nugget pile in a leather tray reads as generic treasure, not clearly Wild West/Gold Rush. Also, soft waves are not a valid category 3 treatment.
fix: Replaced with a miner's ore bucket overflowing with ore and gold chunks on a rough camp crate, with a valid category 3 camp backdrop.

problem: The blank claim stake is text-dependent and too generic without a caption; a player may see only a flag on a post.
fix: Replaced with a timber mine portal with chunky rails and a gold pile at the mouth, placed in the bright creekside Gold Rush camp.

problem: OK: wide-brim prospector hat with chin cord and nugget pin reads frontier/Gold Rush.
OK: balance scale weighing nuggets is a clear Gold Rush camp device and sits logically on an assay crate.
